title: MALAWI: Catholic University Renews USD 576,036.87 Fundraising Drive to Support Needy Students
desc:
By Luke Bisani
The Catholic University of Malawi (CUNIMA) has renewed its drive to raise USD 576,036.87 for its Endowment Fund, aimed at supporting the needy and deserving students to access and complete their higher education.
Speaking during a press conference organised by the University this week, Deputy Vice Chancellor Rev. Fr. Dr. Raphael Mkuzi said that despite being a private institution, CUNIMA has a significant number of students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds who struggle to meet the costs of higher education.
“Many people think that because we are a private university, we only enrol students from well-to-do families. However, this is not the case. We have academically capable students who struggle to meet their tuition fees and other educational expenses, thereby finding it difficult to access the education we offer,” Fr. Mkuzi said.
He explained that the initiative is rooted in the principles of Catholic Social Teaching, particularly the preferential option for the poor, which calls on the University to prioritise the needs of disadvantaged members of society.
“Guided by the teachings of the Church, which we also impart to our students through Catholic Social Teaching, we are challenged to give preference to the poor. This initiative started some years ago, and we are now intensifying our efforts to raise the required funds through various activities and engagements with different stakeholders,” he added.
Fr. Mkuzi disclosed that the University intends to generate an annual budget of USD 120,967.74 from the endowments to support the 100 needy and deserving students with tuition fees and accommodation. He further explained that the fund will be invested to generate sustainable returns, allowing it to continue supporting students over the years.
The Deputy Vice Chancellor therefore appealed to the corporate sector, development partners, individuals and other well-wishers to support the University's fundraising efforts, particularly through the forthcoming charity golf tournament scheduled for 27 November 2026 at the Blantyre Sports Club.
Speaking at the same event, Students' Union Leader Wongani Kings Chidumula commended the University for establishing the Endowment Fund, describing it as an important intervention that will help many students overcome financial barriers to higher education.
The need for the fund is underscored by the financial challenges faced by students seeking university education. Every year, at least 50 students selected to begin their studies at CUNIMA fail to take up their places due to financial constraints. In addition, approximately 20 students drop out annually because they can no longer afford tuition fees.
Although the University, in collaboration with the Students' Welfare Committee, provides financial assistance to a limited number of needy students each semester, the support remains insufficient to meet the growing demand.
Through the Endowment Fund, CUNIMA seeks to establish a sustainable source of financial assistance that will enable more academically deserving students from disadvantaged backgrounds to pursue their educational aspirations without being held back by financial difficulties.
The initiative reflects the University's commitment to its mission of providing quality and holistic higher education while advancing the Catholic Social Teaching principle of the preferential option for the poor.

title: Space-grown glioblastoma organoids could help advance brain cancer treatments
desc: Glioblastoma (GBM) is the most common malignant primary brain tumor in adults and is one of the most aggressive and deadly forms of cancer. It is difficult for surgeons to fully remove GBM because it often has microscopic "tentacles" that extend from the tumor into healthy brain tissue. GBM is also hard to treat because it creates an immunosuppressive microenvironment that helps the cancer evade immune attack and resist therapy.

title: Drone-based AI system tracks cattle growth without stressful trips to scales
desc: In beef cattle production, determining the ideal time to sell makes all the difference in a producer's costs. This is because, once an animal reaches its natural growth limit, it stops gaining weight significantly. From that point on, every additional day in a feedlot means spending money on feed without gaining meat in return.

title: Gold prices plunge to one-year low below $3,900 as higher oil prices fuel fears of more pain ahead
desc: (Kitco News) - The gold market has taken a big hit heading into the weekend, with prices breaking convincingly below $4,000 an ounce and falling to their lowest levels in more than a year.Gold's sharp selloff Friday pushed prices to their lowest level since October 6, 2025, when the precious metal touched an intraday low of $3,884.61 an ounce. The latest decline comes as investors brace for another potentially volatile week, with U.S. employment data and the midterm elections expected to provide fresh uncertainty for financial markets.According to analysts and traders, there is significant frustration in the marketplace as gold faces substantial selling pressure even as the U.S. dollar and bond yields weaken. (Kitco Global Index shows how much of today's gold move is the dollar versus the gold market itself.) Traditionally, these two factors should be bullish for the precious metal, as they reduce its opportunity costs.Spot gold last traded at $3,880 an ounce, down 3.5% on the day; prices are down nearly 3% on the week. Silver is experiencing an even bigger drop, with prices falling below $50 an ounce. Spot silver last traded at $48.95 an ounce, down nearly 6% on the day. Silver prices are down nearly 9% since last Friday, marking their worst weekly decline since early June.Analysts have said that gold has been unable to find any bullish traction, even with lower bond yields, because of broader concerns in the marketplace.Although the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged following its monetary policy meeting Wednesday, the central bank remains committed to bringing inflation down. Looking beyond this week's pause, markets still expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December and through the first quarter of 2027.Philip Streible, Chief Market Strategist at Blue Line Futures, said that gold will continue to struggle as the ongoing war with Iran keeps oil prices elevated.“The rule in the markets is that you are supposed to buy the inflation and oil right now is the inflation,” he said.Streible added that gold performs well when the central bank is forced to cut interest rates to support the economy. However, with the economy expanding by 3.4% in the third quarter, he said the U.S. central bank has plenty of room to raise rates.“If the economy stays strong the Fed can continue to raise interest rates, which means gold will continue to have a target on its back,” he said.Simon-Peter Massabni, Head of Business Development at XS.com, said that despite the weakness in the U.S. dollar and lower bond yields, gold is reacting to inflation expectations and the future path of interest rates.“The decisive factor will be whether incoming economic data prompt markets to reassess the interest-rate outlook, shifting expectations toward a pause in tightening or a resumption of rate cuts. Until then, gold is likely to remain under selling pressure, despite supportive factors that continue to underpin its medium- to long-term outlook,” he said.“I see three developments that could change the outlook. First, a gradual but clear cooling in the US labor market, reflected in weaker job growth, rising unemployment, and slower wage growth. Second, a sustained decline in inflation, particularly core inflation and price components that capture the pass-through of higher energy costs into broader goods and services. Third, a downward repricing of future interest rate expectations and real yields.”Looking at gold's technical price action, Waleed Said, Technical Analyst at GivTrade, said that the path of least resistance remains lower. He added that he expects gold prices to eventually test support at $3,800 an ounce.The latest selloff has also pushed gold significantly below its 200-day moving average, which stands near $4,490 an ounce. With prices trading roughly 13.5% below this long-term trend indicator, the technical picture continues to reflect significant bearish momentum.“The mechanism matters here. It is not that people are swapping their gold for oil,” Said said. “Higher oil means higher inflation, higher inflation keeps central banks hawkish. On top of that, when the tech selloff hit, people sold gold to cover margin calls elsewhere. Gold is liquid, so it is the first thing that gets sold when people need cash. So in this war gold is not acting as the safe haven people expect. Oil and the dollar are taking that role.”With all the attention on inflation and oil prices, Naeem Aslam, CIO of Zaye Capital Markets, said that next week's midterm elections could have an impact on the outlook.Some political analysts have said that if Democrats regain control of Congress, winning majorities in both the House and Senate, it could become more difficult for the Trump administration to continue its war with Iran.Analysts have said that anything that eases tensions in the Middle East and ends the global energy supply crunch could be positive for gold.Aslam said he still expects any major dip in gold prices to represent a long-term buying opportunity.Jeff Sarti, CEO of Morton Wealth, said that he also sees a buying opportunity for gold, as the latest selloff appears to be a technical move.“DSI sentiment is flashing very bearish, which from a contrarian point of view indicates that this may be a strong entry point,” he said.Sarti added that he is also not concerned about gold's broken correlation with bond yields over the past week.“Much of the reason why yields are moderating is that there has been a sentiment shift away from the mega cap tech stocks into the safety net of bonds. But, the counter is that the latest GDP data was strong, implying that bond yields should be higher as opposed to lower. So, I think that there is some short-term noise, tied to stock market sentiment, pushing bond yields lower, as opposed to the assumption that the odds of interest rate hikes are moderating,” he said.Looking ahead, investors will have plenty of potential catalysts to navigate as financial markets remain volatile. Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections could have significant implications for the ongoing conflict with Iran and the outlook for energy prices, while Friday's nonfarm payrolls report will provide an important update on the health of the U.S. labor market.With gold struggling to attract safe-haven demand and inflation concerns keeping the Federal Reserve on a tightening path, analysts expect the precious metal to remain sensitive to shifting interest-rate expectations and broader market sentiment.Economic data to watch next week:Monday: ISM Manufacturing PMITuesday: US JOLTS job openings, mid-term electionsWednesday: ADP nonfarm payrolls, ISM Services PMIThursday: Bank of England monetary policy meeting, US weekly jobless claimsFriday: US nonfarm payrolls, University of Michigan preliminary Consumer Sentiment surveySee live precious metals prices for gold, silver, platinum and palladium — in USD, CAD and 12 more currencies.
